answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy works best through expensive, non-transferable identity anchors. Before an agent can vouch or transact, it must lock a copper-denominated bond in escrow that is slashed if a peer audit proves it fake, and each identity must also carry a verified human or hardware anchor. Creating a thousand ghosts then requires a thousand real bonds, so the attacker's cost scales linearly while any single failed audit burns the whole set. Like a glacier, this edge accrues slowly but never melts back into free identities.
